data.narrative:
Physical Intelligence, a Series B AI & Software company founded by Hausman, Levine, Finn, and Ichter, is valued at $5.6B post-money following $600M+ in total capital raised. The relevant peer universe comprises 1 public company (Palantir) and 8 private firms at similar or adjacent stages, including Figure AI ($39.0B, Series C), Scale AI ($29.0B, Series B), and Reflection AI ($25.0B, Series A).

Two valuation methods anchor the analysis. Stage-progression methodology applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage advancement, implying $10.6B. Peer-median analysis across 7 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median of $14.0B, with a range spanning $3.2B to $39.0B. The wide dispersion reflects heterogeneous stage distribution and funding momentum across the AI & Software frontier-tech cohort.

Triangulation of both methods supports a valuation range of $9.0B (low) to $16.1B (high), with a median of $12.3B. This implies 15–40% upside from current post-money valuation. Key uncertainties include competitive positioning relative to Figure AI and Scale AI, which command significantly higher valuations at comparable or proximate stages, and the degree to which recent fundraising velocity and model performance materiality justify premium-to-peer multiples. The current $5.6B valuation appears conservative relative to stage-adjusted peer medians but warrants scrutiny of company-specific differentiation and revenue traction.
